mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI inflation index exceeds 2.5, it triggers concerns about rising prices, prompting central banks to raise interest rates, which reduces equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not decline significantly when CPIAUCSL crosses above 2.5, or returns revert to positive within the same period.

mechanism_narrative: Conflicting signals between falling federal funds rates and rising unemployment rates create market uncertainty, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days when both conditions occur simultaneously.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite both FEDFUNDS < 2% and UNRATE rising > 0.1pp in the same period.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, simultaneous growth in both demand (GDPC1) and supply (INDPRO) indicators signals overexpansion, prompting market corrections and negative returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day rolling window shows positive returns > 60% of baseline during late-cycle periods, or no significant correlation between GDPC1/INDPRO growth and returns.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (UNRATE >4%) paired with stable employment (PAYEMS >5,000) creates a risk of rate hikes, leading to negative S&P 500 returns within 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4% and PAYEMS remains above 5.0
failure_condition: 20-day returns remain positive despite UNRATE >4% and PAYEMS >5,000 in the same period.

mechanism_narrative: Significant declines in both demand (GDPC1) and supply (INDPRO) indicators suggest economic contraction, causing market pessimism and negative returns within 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls 2% and INDPRO falls 5% in a month
regime_hint: contraction in both demand and supply
failure_condition: 5-day returns do not decline significantly when both GDPC1 and INDPRO fall by their respective thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: Extremely low federal funds rates (<1%) alongside robust demand growth (HOUST) signal accommodative policy and strong market conditions, driving positive S&P 500 returns within 5 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% and HOUST rises 5% in a month
regime_hint: extremely accommodative monetary policy and strong demand
failure_condition: 5-day returns remain negative despite FEDFUNDS <1% and HOUST rising 5% in the same period.

mechanism_narrative: Post-shock recovery periods marked by falling federal funds rates and improving labor conditions (UNRATE) foster optimism, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day rolling window shows no significant positive returns during post-shock recovery periods defined by FEDFUNDS decline and UNRATE improvement.
